name: Syndactyly Type 6

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Syndactyly Type 6

criteria.description: Complete or partial soft tissue and/or bony fusion of the third and fourth fingers
Radiographic evidence of osseous syndactyly between affected digits
Lack of associated systemic malformations or syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical syndactyly involving digits 3 and 4 confirmed by radiographic evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete soft tissue syndactyly of the third and fourth fingers
searchTerms: full soft tissue fusion of 3rd and 4th fingers
complete skin joining between middle and ring fingers

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bony fusion between middle and ring phalanges of the hand
searchTerms: bone fusion between middle and ring finger bones
bony connection of adjacent finger phalanges

common.symptomName: Limited independent finger movement between fused digits
searchTerms: limited finger movement between fused digits

common.symptomName: Normal skin texture over syndactylous webbing
searchTerms: normal skin feel over webbed fingers
nail changes where fingers are joined

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness in affected fingers
Cosmetic concerns related to finger appearance

rare.symptomName: Associated mild syndromic features such as craniofacial anomalies
Presence of additional digital anomalies (e.g., polydactyly)

imaging: X-ray demonstrating osseous fusion between phalanges of digits 3 and 4
Radiographs showing absence of other skeletal abnormalities
genetic: Possible mutations in genes associated with limb development (e.g., HOXD13) though not consistently identified
other: Physical examination revealing syndactyly limited to third and fourth fingers without systemic involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement primarily of second and third digits

redFlags: Presence of syndactyly involving multiple digits beyond 3 and 4
Associated systemic malformations suggesting syndromic diagnosis
Progressive joint stiffness or functional impairment
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
